q: A solution has a pH of 11.4 at 25°C. What is the hydroxide ion concentration [OH⁻] in mol/dm³?
A gas occupies 400 cm³ at 27°C and 750 mmHg. What volume will it occupy at s.t.p. (0°C, 760 mmHg)?
How many structural isomers exist for the molecular formula C₄H₉Br?
explain: 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane, and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.

q: What mass of copper is deposited when 2.5 A flows through CuSO₄ solution for 5790 seconds? (Cu = 63.5, F = 96500 C/mol)
Which tran ion combination forms the most thermodynamically stable complex?
opts: Hard acid with hard base (e.g., Ti⁴⁺ with F⁻)
Soft acid with hard base (e.g., Pt²⁺ with H₂O)
Hard acid with soft base (e.g., Na⁺ with I⁻)
Hard base with soft acid in aqueous solution
explain: The HSAB principle states that hard acids prefer to coordinate with hard bases, and soft acids prefer soft bases, forming ionic/electrostatic interactions for hard-hard pairs and covalent interactions for soft-soft pairs.

q: Which of the following statements best explains why the first ionization energy of sulfur is lower than that of phosphorus?
opts: Sulfur has a larger atomic radius than phosphorus
Paired electrons in the 3p orbital of sulfur experience increased inter-electronic repulsion
Phosphorus has a completely filled valence shell
Sulfur exhibits greater nuclear shielding due to d-orbital electrons
explain: Phosphorus has a half-filled 3p³ subshell, whereas sulfur has a 3p⁴ configuration where two electrons occupy the same 3p orbital, creating electrostatic repulsion that lowers the energy required to remove one electron.

q: What is the major product obtained from the hydroboration-oxidation of 1-methylcyclohexene?
explain: Hydroboration-oxidation proceeds via concerted syn-addition of H and BH₂ to the less sterically hindered carbon, followed by oxidation with retention of configuration, yielding trans-2-methylcyclohexanol.

q: Calculate the pH of a 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ mol/dm³ aqueous solution of HCl at 25 °C. (K_w = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴)
explain: At ultra-low acid concentrations, autoionization of water contributes significantly: [H⁺]² - 10⁻⁸[H⁺] - 10⁻¹⁴ = 0, giving [H⁺] ≈ 1.05 × 10⁻⁷ mol/dm³ and pH = -log(1.05 × 10⁻⁷) ≈ 6.98.

q: In mass spectrometry, what is the primary driving force behind the McLafferty rearrangement in carbonyl compounds?
opts: Loss of a stable radical cation
Six-membered cyclic transition state transfer of a γ-hydrogen to the carbonyl oxygen, eliminating a neutral alkene
Direct cleavage of the alpha carbon-carbon bond
Formation of a four-membered cyclic oxetane ring
explain: Carbonyl compounds containing a γ-hydrogen undergo cleavage of the α-β bond via a favorable six-membered cyclic transition state, expelling a neutral alkene molecule and forming an enol radical cation.

q: Which complex ion is diamagnetic and exhibits an octahedral geometry?
explain: In [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, Co³⁺ is a d⁶ ion and NH₃ acts as a strong-field ligand, forcing all six electrons to pair in the lower-energy t₂g orbitals (t₂g⁶ e_g⁰), resulting in zero unpaired electrons (diamagnetic).

q: For a zero-order reaction A → Products with rate constant k = 0.025 mol/(dm³·s) and initial concentration [A]₀ = 0.50 mol/dm³, how long does it take for 80% of the reactant to be consumed?
explain: 80% consumption means 0.40 mol/dm³ reacts, leaving 0.10 mol/dm³. For zero-order kinetics, t = ([A]₀ - [A]) / k = 0.40 / 0.025 = 16 s.

q: Which of the following reagents selectively oxidizes an allylic or benzylic alcohol to the corresponding aldehyde or ketone without affecting isolated saturated alcohols?
explain: Activated MnO₂ is a mild, chemoselective oxidizing agent that oxidizes allylic and benzylic alcohols via a radical intermediate stabilized by conjugation.

q: Determine the crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) in terms of Δ_o (excluding pairing energy) for a high-spin d⁶ octahedral complex.
explain: A high-spin d⁶ configuration is t₂g⁴ e_g². CFSE = 4(-0.4 Δ_o) + 2(+0.6 Δ_o) = -1.6 Δ_o + 1.2 Δ_o = -0.4 Δ_o.

q: What is the stereochemical outcome of the thermal electrocyclic ring closure of (2E,4Z,6E)-octa-2,4,6-triene?
explain: According to Woodward-Hoffmann rules, a 6π-electron conjugated system undergoes thermal electrocyclic ring closure via a disrotatory motion, placing both terminal methyl groups cis to each other.

q: Which thermodynamic relation is valid for an ideal gas undergoing a reversible isothermal expansion?
explain: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends solely on temperature (ΔU = 0 at constant T). By the first law, q = -w = nRT ln(V₂/V₁).

q: Why does pyrrole undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution predominantly at the C-2 (alpha) position rather than C-3 (beta)?
opts: C-2 is less sterically hindered than C-3
Attack at C-2 generates a carbocation intermediate stabilized by three resonance contributors, whereas C-3 attack yields only two
The nitrogen atom withdraws electron density inductively from C-3
C-2 forms an anti-aromatic transition state
explain: Electrophilic attack at C-2 allows delocalization of the positive charge across three resonance structures without disrupting the aromatic sextet as severely as C-3 attack, which only permits two resonance forms.

q: What is the bond angle and hybridization of the central xenon atom in xenon tetrafluoride (XeF₄)?
explain: XeF₄ has 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs (steric number 6), corresponding to sp³d² hybridization with a square planar molecular geometry and 90° F-Xe-F bond angles.

q: Calculate the ionic strength (I) of an aqueous solution containing 0.10 mol/dm³ NaCl and 0.20 mol/dm³ CaCl₂.
In NMR spectroscopy, why does the aldehydic proton (-CHO) appear far downfield around 9.5–10.0 ppm?
opts: Strong electron donation by the alkyl group
Magnetic anisotropy of the carbonyl π-bond combined with inductive deshielding by the electronegative oxygen atom
Hydrogen bonding with the NMR solvent
explain: The induced magnetic field generated by circulating π-electrons in the C=O bond reinforces the external magnetic field in the region of the aldehydic proton, strongly deshielding it alongside inductive withdrawal.

q: Which of the following oxides exhibits amphoteric behavior by reacting with both strong acids and strong alkalis?
explain: Beryllium oxide (BeO) displays diagonal similarity to aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃), reacting with acids to form Be²⁺ salts and with concentrated alkalis to form beryllate ions, [Be(OH)₄]²⁻.

q: What is the major product when cyclohexanone reacts with ethylmagnesium bromide followed by acidic workup?
explain: Grignard reagents act as strong carbon nucleophiles that attack the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, yielding a tertiary alcohol (1-ethylcyclohexanol) upon protonation.

q: Which quantum mechanical principle states that no two electrons in an atom can have the exact same set of four quantum numbers?
explain: The Pauli exclusion principle dictates that an atomic orbital can hold at most two electrons, and they must have opposite spins (m_s = +½ and -½).

q: In the contact process for sulfuric acid manufacture, why is sulfur trioxide (SO₃) absorbed in concentrated H₂SO₄ rather than directly in water?
opts: SO₃ is completely insoluble in water
Direct reaction with water is highly exothermic and produces a dense corrosive mist of sulfuric acid droplets that is difficult to condense
Water decomposes SO₃ back into SO₂ and O₂
Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a catalyst for the oxidation of SO₂
explain: Dissolving SO₃ directly in water releases immense heat that vaporizes water into an uncontrollable acid fog; absorbing it in 98% H₂SO₄ safely forms oleum (H₂S₂O₇).

q: What is the hybridization of each boron atom in diborane (B₂H₆)?
explain: Each boron atom in B₂H₆ is bonded to two terminal hydrogens via normal 2c-2e bonds and two bridging hydrogens via 3c-2e banana bonds, adopting a distorted tetrahedral (sp³) geometry.

q: Which catalyst is employed in the Ziegler-Natta polymerization of ethene to produce high-density polyethylene (HDPE)?
explain: Ziegler-Natta catalysts consist of a transition metal halide (such as TiCl₄) and an organoaluminum co-catalyst, enabling stereoregular linear polymerization at low temperatures and pressures.

q: Determine the standard enthalpy of reaction (ΔH°_rxn) for C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g), given bond dissociation energies: C=C (614 kJ/mol), C-C (348 kJ/mol), H-H (436 kJ/mol), and C-H (413 kJ/mol).
explain: ΔH = Σ(Bonds broken) - Σ(Bonds formed) = [614 + 436] - [348 + 2(413)] = 1050 - 1174 = -124 kJ/mol.

q: Which of the following molecules has a non-zero net dipole moment?
explain: ClF₃ has 3 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs on the central chlorine atom, adopting an asymmetric T-shaped geometry where bond dipoles do not cancel.

q: What is the role of cryolite (Na₃AlF₆) in the electrolytic extraction of aluminum from purified bauxite?
opts: It oxidizes impurities such as iron(III) oxide
It lowers the melting point of alumina from ~2050 °C to ~950 °C and increases electrical conductivity
It prevents the carbon anodes from burning in oxygen
It reduces Al³⁺ ions chemically before electrolysis
explain: Adding molten cryolite dissolves Al₂O₃ at a much lower operating temperature, drastically reducing energy costs and enhancing ionic conductivity.

q: During the ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene followed by reductive workup with dimethyl sulfide (Me₂S), what products are formed?
explain: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C double bond into two carbonyl fragments: the disubstituted carbon yields propanone (acetone), while the monosubstituted carbon yields ethanal (acetaldehyde).

q: Which phenomenon explains why a colloidal sol scatters a beam of visible light passing through it?
explain: The Tyndall effect occurs when dispersed colloidal particles have dimensions comparable to the wavelength of visible light, causing scattering.

q: In acid-base titrations, why is phenolphthalein unsuitable as an indicator for titrating a weak base (like NH₃) with a strong acid (like HCl)?
opts: Its pH transition range (8.2–10.0) lies completely above the acidic equivalence point (pH ~5.3)
It forms an insoluble precipitate with ammonium ions
It has no color change in aqueous media
explain: The equivalence point of a weak base-strong acid titration falls in the acidic region (pH 4–6), where methyl orange (3.1–4.4) is required rather than alkaline-range phenolphthalein.

q: What is the rate-determining step in the acid-catalyzed iodination of propanone (CH₃COCH₃)?
opts: Attack of molecular iodine (I₂) on the enol double bond
Tautomerization of the keto form to the enol form
explain: The reaction rate is zero-order with respect to iodine concentration because the slow, rate-determining step is the acid-catalyzed enolization of propanone.

q: Which lanthanide ion is colorless in aqueous solution due to having an empty 4f subshell?
explain: La³⁺ has a [Xe] 4f⁰ electron configuration with no f-electrons available for f-f electronic transitions, rendering its aqueous solutions colorless.

q: What happens to the boiling point of water when the external atmospheric pressure is reduced from 101.3 kPa to 50 kPa?
opts: It decreases below 100 °C because vapor pressure equals external pressure at a lower temperature
explain: A liquid boils when its saturated vapor pressure equals the surrounding external pressure; lowering ambient pressure lowers the temperature required to reach that vapor pressure.

q: Which type of isomerism is exhibited by the pair of coordination compounds [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₃ and [Cr(H₂O)₅Cl]Cl₂·H₂O?
explain: Hydrate isomers differ in whether water molecules are directly coordinated to the central metal ion as ligands or held as uncoordinated water of crystallization in the lattice.

q: Which intermediate is generated when chloroform (CHCl₃) reacts with a strong base such as potassium tert-butoxide?
explain: Base abstracts the acidic proton from CHCl₃ to give CCl₃⁻, which undergoes α-elimination of Cl⁻ to form singlet dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂).

q: Calculate the pH of a 0.050 mol/dm³ solution of sodium acetate (CH₃COONa) at 25 °C. (K_a of CH₃COOH = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵)
In the Birch reduction of anisole (methoxybenzene) using sodium in liquid ammonia and ethanol, what is the major product?
explain: Electron-donating groups like -OCH₃ stabilize radical anion intermediates at meta/ortho positions, leaving the methoxy-bearing carbon unreduced to give 1-methoxycyclohexa-1,4-diene.

q: Which of the following is the correct order of decreasing basicity of methyl-substituted amines in aqueous solution?
explain: In aqueous phase, a balance of positive inductive effect (+I), steric hindrance, and solvation stabilization of the conjugate ammonium cation makes secondary dimethylamine the strongest base.

q: What is the number of radial nodes present in a 4p atomic orbital?
explain: The number of radial (spherical) nodes is given by n - l - 1. For a 4p orbital, n = 4 and l = 1, giving 4 - 1 - 1 = 2 radial nodes.

q: Which reagent is used in the Wolff-Kishner reduction to convert an aldehyde or ketone directly into an alkane?
opts: Hydrazine (NH₂NH₂) and KOH in ethylene glycol with heat
explain: The Wolff-Kishner reduction converts carbonyl groups into methylene (-CH₂-) groups under strongly basic conditions via hydrazone formation and extrusion of N₂ gas.

q: Why does white phosphorus (P₄) ignite spontaneously in air at room temperature whereas red phosphorus does not?
opts: White phosphorus has higher molar mass
White phosphorus possesses severe angle strain (60° bond angles) in discrete P₄ tetrahedra, making it highly reactive
Red phosphorus is coated with an oxide layer
White phosphorus is an ionic solid
explain: The 60° P-P-P bond angles in discrete P₄ molecules introduce substantial ring strain, lowering the activation energy for oxidation compared to polymeric red phosphorus.

q: During the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous copper(II) sulfate using copper electrodes, what happens to the concentration of Cu²⁺ ions in the electrolyte?
opts: It decreases steadily until the solution turns colorless
It remains virtually constant because copper dissolves from the anode at the same rate it deposits on the cathode
explain: Active copper electrodes participate in the redox process: Cu(s) → Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ at the anode balances Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s) at the cathode.

q: Which of the following compounds undergoes decarboxylation most readily upon gentle heating?
explain: β-Keto acids like 3-oxobutanoic acid decarboxylate easily upon mild heating via a concerted six-membered cyclic transition state, yielding an enol that tautomerizes to a ketone.

q: What is the packing efficiency of atoms in a body-centered cubic (BCC) crystal lattice?
explain: A BCC unit cell contains 2 atoms with edge length a = 4r/√3. Packing efficiency = [2 × (4/3)πr³] / (4r/√3)³ = (π√3)/8 ≈ 68.0%.
